set.body:
Point 3 and producer half of point 4. Repository owner: StoryModel; boundaries: existing core/recall/align/view/codec/fixtures modules and a narrowly scoped pipeline writer if needed. No new top-level module. Governing charter: docs/refactor/goals/source-recall-workspace-m1-20260922.md. Existing Atlas proposal crosswalk: AT-03/04/10 and provider portions of AT-08/24.

Prerequisite: G1 checked mapping records, which already depends on support honesty. Reuse BundleManifest/output identities and public codecs where suitable; do not invent a second mapping ontology. G1's reserved Derived/Calibrated tags remain unavailable.

Deliverables and acceptance:
1. A thin versioned manifest with exact byte digests and semantic join bindings for source edition/model, recall inventory/segmentation, mapping, derivation/receipts, optional features and content capabilities. Digests establish identity, never grant access. Distinguish supplied, absent, refused and unauthorized artifacts; optional missing features/media do not erase valid mapping.
2. Checked source/recall/mapping joins reject a foreign source or recall even with reused titles/local IDs, a tampered sidecar, unsupported version and inconsistent unit inventory before a view is compiled. A changed source/recall changes the bound identity. Imported/draft authority and gaps remain intact.
3. A provider-owned minimal matrix projection at ONE explicit fixed target cut: all requested recall outcomes, ordered target dictionary, supplied values with measure kind/normalization/candidate coverage, external alternatives, processing failures/abstentions/unresolved status, decision origin, exact source/recall evidence and navigation addresses. Never renormalize after filtering; omitted candidate probability remains unknown. Processing failure is not a probability destination. No parent/child aggregation or time interpolation is required for M1.
4. Provider-owned resolve/inverse-query and deterministic permitted selection-subset/table/text-twin operations. Preserve repeated references and discontiguous support. Selection export exposes the same IDs, values and policy as inspection; the UI performs no scientific arithmetic.
5. A reproducible offline generator using public construction/codec paths for a serialized WOG source/recall/mapping case and a small structurally different synthetic text case. Include partial/draft, untimed, all-external, missing evidence, failed unit and raw/decode-disagreement witnesses; expose synthetic status. Reuse G1 miniature expectations where applicable. An independent expected-answer file lists exact IDs, support, values and unit counts. No requirement to create automatic scenes or parse real recall charts.
6. Exact large integer coordinates/timebases survive JS decoding where present; no timestamp inferred for an untimed unit. Privacy denial excludes content from compiled payload, DOM-facing labels, tooltips, twins, exports and diagnostics.

Falsifiers: change one digest while keeping title/IDs; drop one failed/untimed row; exchange source/recall bindings; renormalize source-only values; turn absence into zero; include a denied string in an export; substitute a hull for exact support. Each must fail a named court with an accepting control.

Handoff: publish the exact reachable provider commit, schema versions, generator command, fixture digests, expected answers and gate receipts. Notify no person automatically; add the evidence to the linked Atlas adoption issue when working that store. That issue remains blocked until this concrete provider package is inspectable, then the next implementer opens and runs its consumer gate.

Evidence: scoped JVM/JS/Native tests and named failing mutations with passing controls; separate SD6 review; clean merge-result sbt -batch checkAll with bound test-task totals, exit, exact SHA and preserved goldens. Run tools/reference-scope.sh on the actual diff and exact-pin consumer checks for changed consumed APIs. Public vocabulary requires the corresponding ADR line. No scientific efficacy, calibration, hosted CI or publication claim follows from local tests.
set.title: [M1] Publish checked workspace packet, fixed-cut matrix and acceptance fixtures
